newsitem.title: UK: Monthly review - Zaire's Mobutu forced into talks.
newsitem.headline: Monthly review - Zaire's Mobutu forced into talks.

text.p: The relentless advance of Laurent Kabila's rebels throughout April forced ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko to finally agree to peace talks.

The Peruvian hostage crisis ended after 126 days when government troops stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, killing all 14 Marxist rebels and rescuing 71 of the 72 hostages. One hostage and three soldiers died in the assault.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
Apr 1 - Pakistani parliament passes a constitutional amendment bill to curb presidential powers to sack a government and parliament.
Apr 1 - Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino makes his first visit to the rebel-held south since insurgents seized control of the region last month.
Apr 1 - Two Palestinians killed in explosions in the Gaza Strip which Israel says were suicide bombings; PLO blames Israeli troops.
Apr 2 - Russia and Belarus sign an outline Union Treaty but agree to rework the details after 11th-hour intervention by liberals in Moscow.

Apr 2 - Zairean President Mobutu appoints his arch-rival Etienne Tshisekedi prime minister. On the 3rd Tshisekedi offers the rebels six cabinet posts but they reject the offer. On the 8th Mobutu declares a state of emergency. On the 9th Mobutu appoints General Likulia Bolongo prime minister, replacing Tshisekedi.
Apr 3 - German Chancellor Helmut Kohl announces he will stand for re-election in 1998 for an unprecedented fifth term.
Apr 3 - U.N. Security Council announces its peacekeepers will leave Haiti after mandate expires on July 31.
Apr 3 - Brazil's Senate approves bill classifying torture as a crime, three days after the TV airing of a video showing police beating civilians.
Apr 4 - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu offers a Camp David-style meeting with U.S. and Palestinian leaders.
Apr 5 - Yemen publicly executes a man who shot dead four children and two teachers.
Apr 5 - On the day Zairean rebels and government representatives meet for peace talks in South Africa, rebel forces occupy the diamond-mining town of Mbuji-Mayi.
Apr 5 - Britain's Grand National horse race is postponed after a bomb alert. The race is eventually run on April 7. IRA claims responsibility for the security alert.
Apr 6 - Suspected Kashmiri militants plant a bomb on a bus in the Punjab, killing two and injuring 14.
Apr 6 - Bomb explodes at the house of one of Burma's top military officials, killing his daughter and setting off a renewed security alert in Rangoon.
Apr 8 - The Non-Aligned Movement urges member states to freeze diplomatic ties with Israel at existing levels.
Apr 8 - U.S. space shuttle Columbia ends mission due to faulty power generator, less than four days after blasting off.
Apr 9 - Iraq flies 104 Moslem pilgrims to Saudi Arabia for the haj pilgrimage in an apparent attempt to use religious grounds to defy a U.N. air embargo.
Apr 9 - Albania's main opposition Socialist Party returns to parliament nearly a year after it abandoned its seats charging widespread election fraud.
Apr 9 - India and Pakistan hold talks amid rising hopes they will be able to defuse half a century of tensions.
Apr 9 - Italy's lower house of parliament votes overwhelmingly in favour of deploying an Italian-led security force to Albania.
Apr 9 - Zairean rebels enter the country's second city and mining capital Lubumbashi.
Apr 9 - Radical Chechen guerrilla commander Salman Raduyev, one of Russia's most wanted men, is critically injured in an assassination attempt.

Apr 10 - German court accuses Iran of ordering the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin, causing a round of tit-for-tat expulsions. On April 29 European Union foreign ministers agree that ambassadors called home from Tehran could return if their governments wish.
Apr 10 - Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi wins a confidence vote in the Senate over Albania.
Apr 11 - Turin Cathedral is engulfed by flames but the famous Turin shroud is saved by firemen.
Apr 11 - Angola swears in a government of national unity bringing together former foes from 19 years of civil war.
Apr 11 - Italian soldiers arrive in Albania to spearhead a multinational force.
Apr 11 - The European Commission says it has struck a deal with the U.S. settling their trade dispute over the U.S.'s Helms-Burton anti-Cuba legislation.
Apr 12 - Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda tenders his resignation and is asked to remain as caretaker prime minister.
Apr 12 - Albania's King Leka I returns home after 58 years in exile and says restoration of the monarchy could unify the country.
Apr 12 - Pope John Paul appeals for tolerance in Bosnia only hours after police removed explosives planted on his motorcade route into Sarajevo.
Apr 13 - Zairean rebels say they are restarting the civil war against the Kinshasa-based government after a three-day pause and demand the resignation of President Mobutu.
Apr 14 - Former SS captain Erich Priebke, accused of involvement in Italy's worst World War Two massacre, goes on trial in Rome for the second time.
Apr 15 - Nearly 1,200 French, Italian and Spanish troops arrive in Albania at the port of Durres to safeguard humanitarian aid.
Apr 15 - Three hundred and forty-three Moslem haj pilgrims die when fire rips through a tent compound near Mecca. At least 1,500 are injured.
Apr 16 - European mediation arranges a meeting between PLO leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign minister David Levy in Malta.
Apr 19 - India's United Front names Inder Kumar Gujral as its new leader. The next day he is chosen as prime minister and sworn in on the 21st.
Apr 19 - The first ship to sail directly to Taiwan from China in 48 years steams into Kaohsiung port. A Taiwanese ship makes the reverse journey April 24-25.
Apr 20 - North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop arrives in South Korea from the Philippines.
Apr 20 - Israeli prosecutors decide not to charge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal but indict a key coalition ally.
Apr 21 - An advance contingent of Chinese troops enters Hong Kong to prepare garrison facilities for the July 1st handover.
Apr 21 - The ashes of 1960s LSD guru Timothy Leary and "Star Trek" creator Gene Roddenberry are blasted into space in the world's first space funeral.
Apr 21 - French President Jacques Chirac dissolves parliament and calls early elections for May 25 and June 1.
Apr 22 - Algerian government says Moslem rebels killed 93 people in an overnight raid on a village south of Algiers.
Apr 22 - Iraqi helicopters arrive at the southern border with Saudi Arabia to pick up Moslem pilgrims, ignoring a U.S. warning not to violate the "no-fly zone" enforced since the Gulf War.
Apr 22 - President Bill Clinton announces fresh sanctions on Burma, banning new investments by U.S. citizens.
Apr 22 - More than 200,000 elite Iranian troops launch their largest wargames in the Gulf to train for surprise attacks by "enemies".
Apr 22 - Peruvian troops storm the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, freeing 71 hostages. One hostage, three soldiers and all 14 guerrillas killed.
Apr 23 - The presidents of Russia and China sign a declaration opposing the domination of one superpower in the post-Cold War world.
Apr 23 - South African white rightist leader Eugene Terre'Blanche convicted of trying to murder a black man and assaulting another.
Apr 23 - Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein agree in talks on the need to revive the stalled Middle East peace process.
Apr 23 - Zaire's rebel forces announce the capture of Bowete, Tshikapa and Ilebo east of the capital Kinshasa.
Apr 23 - President Bill Clinton meets the Dalai Lama and says he will urge China to open a direct dialogue with the exiled Tibetan leader.
Apr 24 - Trial begins of Timothy McVeigh, accused of the Oklahoma City bombing of April 1995.
Apr 24 - The presidents of Russia, China, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan sign a pact on troop reductions along the former Sino-Soviet border.
Apr 24 - A Bosnian Serb court jails seven Bosnian Moslems after a murder trial which the international community had labelled a farce.
Apr 25 - U.N. agencies accuse Zairean rebels of trying to achieve a "final solution" by allowing thousands of Hutu refugees to die a slow and cruel death.
Apr 25 - Kim Hyun-chul, son of South Korean president Kim Young-sam, answers questions in a parliamentary inquisition into a loans-for-kickbacks scandal.
Apr 25 - The Peruvian government strongly denies reports that troops executed some rebels when they ended the Lima siege.
Apr 26 - Fire sweeps through the Imperial Hotel, Cotabato, Philippines, killing 25.
Apr 27 - A Yemeni soldier shoots dead eight people during polling in the country's first general election since the 1994 civil war.
Apr 27 - Hong Kong officially opens the world's longest road-rail suspension bridge, linking the colony to its new offshore airport.
Apr 28 - Ecuador's deposed President Abdala Bucaram is granted political asylum in Panama.
Apr 28 - Militiamen massacre 17 schoolgirls and a Belgian nun and wound 14 other girls in attacks on two schools in northwestern Rwanda.
Apr 29 - Former Representative Douglas "Pete" Peterson, a fighter pilot who spent 6-1/2 years as a prisoner of war in Hanoi, is sworn in as the first U.S. ambassador to post-war Vietnam.
Apr 29 - A crowded passenger train ploughs into the back of a stationary train in China's central Hunan province, killing at least 67 people.
Apr 30 - An explosion rips through a weapons store at a military base outside the Albanian capital Tirana, killing at least 27 people.
Apr 30 - Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov survives an assassination attempt which kills two people and injures 60.
Apr 30 - A Turkish court sentences 113 Islamist sect members to three years in prison for challenging the official secularist order.

Notable deaths in April included: Zaki Badr, former Egyptian interior minister (3rd); Vladimir Soloukhin, Russian poet and novelist (4); Allen Ginsberg, best known poet of the beat generation (5); Zdenek Mlynar, Czech communist-turned-dissident (15); Emilio Azcarraga Milmo, Mexican media mogul (16); Bijoyananda Patnaik, veteran Indian nationalist (17); Chaim Herzog, former Israeli president (17); Andres Rodriguez, former president of Paraguay (21); Diosdado Macapagal, former Philippines president (21); Denis Compton, legendary English cricketer (23); Peng Zhen, Chinese elder statesman (26).
